Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

can you make a screen reader audit from the notes below for the town library website. keep it to the event calendar and the room booking page, not the whole site. use only what i observed in my test, i didn't check other browsers or screen readers. tested with NVDA and Firefox on Windows 11. on the calendar page, the month heading was announced as plain text, and the next month button was announced as “button” with no name. the list of events had dates, titles and times, but the event links didn't say which event they opened. on room booking, the required fields were marked with an asterisk but there was no explanation of what it meant. after submitting an empty form, the page showed an error message at the top, but focus stayed on the submit button. please explain the issues for someone maintaining the site and suggest a fix for each one. keep the report factual, don't claim you tested anything else or say whether the site passes. output a numbered checklist. for every checklist item put the evidence from my notes before the recommendation, and don't add a separate summary.", "output": "Create a screen-reader audit for the town library website, limited to the event calendar and room booking page. Base the audit only on these observations: testing was conducted with NVDA and Firefox on Windows 11. No other browsers or screen readers were checked.

Observations:
- On the calendar page, the month heading was announced as plain text. The next month button was announced as “button” with no name. Event dates, titles, and times appeared in the list, but the event links did not identify which event they opened.
- On the room booking page, required fields were marked with an asterisk, but there was no explanation of what it meant. After an empty form was submitted, an error message appeared at the top of the page, but focus stayed on the submit button.

Explain each issue for someone maintaining the site and recommend a fix for each one. Keep the report factual. Do not claim to have tested anything else or state whether the site passes. Format the output as a numbered checklist. In every item, present the evidence from the notes before the recommendation. Do not include a separate summary."}]
